caseno:
Death Reference No. 18 of 2006 
With Criminal Appeal No. 2124 of 2006 With Criminal Appeal No.1839 of 2006 With Criminal Appeal No. 1604 of 2006 With Criminal Appeal No. 1606 of 2006 and Jail Appeal No. 198 of 2006.
lawyer:
MA Mannan Mohan, Deputy Attorney-General with Osman Gani, Assistant Attorney-General with Delwara Begum (Bela), Assistant Attorney-General—For the State. 
Baharuddin-al-Razi, Advocate—For the Appellant in Jail Appeal.
parties:
State ------ Appellant
VS.
Samjid Ali ------ Condemned Prisoner.
full_judgment:
5. The prosecution case, as projected in the First Information Report (in short, the FIR) and also unfurled at the time of trial is that deceased Alauddin was an inhabitant of Tarapur village under Gopalgonj Police Station of Sylhet district who like the other days was sleeping in the night following 26-2-2001 in his dwelling building comprising two rooms having two barandas to the eastern side and western side. At 00-30 hours on 27-2-2001 accused Samjid Ali @ Katai, Koyes Ahmed, Joynal Uddin, Mukit, Abedin Ali, Mahmud Ali, Abdus Sattar, Manik, Jamal, Abdul Jabbar, Kalai along with unknown 4 to 5 accused being armed with gun, dagger, dao, iron rod and lathi breaking the door of the eastern side of the building had entered into the room of northern side. Accused Samjid Ali @ Katai fired a blank shot. The inmates of the house being panicked were shouting. Deceased Alauddin who was sleeping in the room of southern side came into the room of northern side while accused Samjid Ali @ Katai made the following utterance to Alauddin. 

 6. Thereafter, accused Koyes Ahmed, Joynal Uddin, Mukit, Abedin Ali, Mahmud Ali pulling up Alauddin brought him in the room of western side of the building where accused Samjid Ali @ Katai fired gun on the right chest of Alauddin causing his instant death. The accused assaulting the inmates of the house asked them to be calm and quiet and left the place of occurrence through the door of eastern side of the house. Hearing the alarm raised by the inmates of the house, the local witnesses coming to the house of occurrence found the occurrence to whom the informant and other inmates of the house narrated the occurrence of murder. Jesmin Akter, the daughter of deceased Alauddin lodged, the FIR with the Golapgonj Police Station and on the basis of the said FIR Golapgonj Police Station Case No. 10 dated 27-2-2001 corresponding to GR No. 19 of 2001 were started. 

 7. The case was investigated by PWs 16 and 17 who after completion of the investigation submitted police report recommending the trial of the accused-persons named in the said report under sections 460/302/34 of the Penal Code and eventually, the accused were put on trial before the Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet where the accused were invited to answer the charges framed against them under sections 302/34/458 and 459 of the Penal Code to which all the accused save and except accused Mukit, Abdul Jabbar and Kalai pleaded their not guilty and claimed to be tried. On the date of framing charge accused Mukit, Abdul Jabbar and Kalai were on the run, as such, their answer on the charge could not be recorded. The said three accused were duly defended by the state defence lawyer. At trial, the prosecution examined 16 witnesses and tendered 1 witness for cross-examination by the defence but the defence did not cross-examine him and the defence examined none. After closure of the evidence, the accused were examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure when they repeated their innocence and disclosed their unwillingness to adduce defence witness save and except absconding accused Mukit, Jabbar and Kalai. 

 9. The learned Judge, on consideration of the evidence on record and the facts and circumstances of the case convicted and sentenced the accused as aforesaid and made the reference under section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for confirmation of sentence of death awarded to accused Samjid Ali @ Katai. Conversely condemned-prisoner Samjid Ali @ Katai being aggrieved by dissatisfied with the judgment and order of conviction and sentence preferred Criminal Appeal No. 1606 of 2006 and Jail Appeal No. 198 of 2006, convict Abdur Rab preferred Criminal Appeal No. 1839 of 2006, convicts Abdul Jabbar and Kalai preferred Criminal Appeal No. 2124 of 2006 and convicts Koyes Ahmed, Joynal Abedin, Abedin Ali, Abdus Sattar, Abdul Manik, Jamal Uddin, Mahmud Ali and Abdur Rab preferred Criminal Appeal No. 1604 of 2006. Abdur Rab has become appellant twice as he alone filed Appeal No. 1839 of 2006 and he is also an appellant in the Appeal No. 1604 of 2006 along with the others. The convict Mukit did not prefer any appeal against the judgment and order of conviction of sentence. 

 10. Mr MA Mannan Mohan, learned Deputy Attorney-General along with Mr Osman Gani Khan and Mrs. Delwara (Bela), Assistant Attorney-Generals appearing on behalf of the state having taken us through the judgment and order under the reference, FIR, the charge, the depositions of the prosecution witnesses, the inquest report and other materials on record makes his submission supporting the reference and opposing the appeals. He submits that the occurrence of murder of deceased Alauddin was taken place in his dwelling house and the murder of the deceased is not disputed at all in this case. The occurrence of murder of the deceased Alauddin has been witnessed by the ocular witnesses who were present in the house of occurrence at the relevant time. He categorically submits that PWs 1, 5, 6, 13 and 14 are the inmates of the house of occurrence who witnessed the occurrence from a close vision and since the occurrence of the murder was taken place at the dead of night at 12-30 AM there had no any possibility and opportunity for others to witness the occurrence. As such, the inmates of the house though they are the son, daughters, wife and son-in-law of the deceased but they are the most probable, competent and natural witnesses of this case. He also submits that immediate after occurrence hearing the alarm raised by the witnesses neighbouring people coming into the place of occurrence heard the occurrence and the names of the accused from the ocular witnesses and without any late on the following morning the FIR was lodged by the informant naming and specifying the role of the accused and the said FIR story has been supported by the eye-witnesses and the witnesses had witnessed the occurrence in the light of the electricity belong to the house and also by the light of torch focus used by the accused. He also submits that PW 7 Juron Begum, the daughter of the deceased was abducted by the accused party before the occurrence of this case and after the arrival of Alauddin in his native house from the abroad he was requested by the accused to withdraw the case filed by his wife for the abduction of said Juron Begum but since the deceased did not withdraw the case, the accused party in order to take revenge of the said case had murdered the deceased. So, the prosecution has also been able to prove the motive of murder of the deceased. The trial court on due consideration of the evidences and other materials on record and the facts and circumstances of the case, rightly found the condemned-prisoner guilty, under section 302 and 459 of the Penal Code and rightly awarded the sentence of death to him and the court below also on due consideration of the evidences and other materials on record found the accused Koyes Ahmed, Joynal Abedin and Abedin Ali guilty under sections 302/34 and 459 of the Penal Code and sentenced them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life with a fine of taka 5,000 each and the other accused bas been rightly found guilty under section 459 of the Penal Code. So the conviction and sentence of the accused calls for no interfere from this Court. Thus according to his submission there is no ground for interfere with the judgment and order of conviction and sentence and with this submission he canvasses for the acceptance of the reference and dismissal of the appeals. 

 11. Conversely Mr Md Baharuddin-al-Razi, the learned Advocate appearing for the condemned-prisoner as well as for the other appellants makes his submission opposing the reference and supporting the Criminal Appeals and Jail Appeal. He submits that the deceased Alauddin was not murdered as alleged by the prosecution. He might have met his death by any other way than that of alleged by the prosecution. He submits that the evidence of the so-called eye-witnesses is not believable at all. All the eye-witnesses are the close relations of the deceased who are the son, daughters, wife and son-in-law of the deceased. More so, in view of the prosecution case itself, those witnesses had no opportunity to witness the occurrence and the murder of the deceased Alauddin. He categorically submits that in view of the prosecution case as projected, the deceased was taken into the room of western side which is known as kitchen also and thereafter he was allegedly murdered by the condemned-prisoner by gun shot but the said room and area of the house is separated from the room of the main house. The witnesses who claimed to have seen the occurrence were either in the northern or southern room of the house. So, they had no scope to be the eye-witnesses of the murder of the deceased. The so-called eye-witnesses had deposed in the trial court like parrot which have been tutored to them to strengthen the prosecution case in the line of FIR. 

 12. He further submits that PW 13 categorically stated that he cannot say from how many distance the gun shot was caused to the deceased but the trial court relying on the evidence of PW 13 also found the accused guilty. He also submits that the medical evidence and the inquest report go to show that there was only one gun shot injury on the persons of the deceased but had there been any occurrence as alleged by the prosecution that the accused party had entered into the house with the dao, rod, lathi, but there appears no marks of violence or other injuries on the persons of the deceased and there is no any case that anybody else of the house in question had sustained any injuries. Had there been any occurrence as alleged by the prosecution, the deceased must have sustained some other injuries on his persons and the other inmates also would have sustained injuries by the accused. So, this fact indicates that the deceased Alauddin was not murdered rather he committed suicide to relive himself from the gloomy and pain of the departure of his daughter Juron Begum against their will. He also submits that prosecution could not examine any independent and disinterested local witness to prove that they had heard the occurrence of murder of the deceased by the accused immediate after occurrence. So, the court below on the wrong assessment of evidence on record illegally convicted and sentenced the condemned-prisoner as well as the other appellants. Therefore the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is not sustainable in law. Thus he canvases for rejection of the reference and to allow the appeals acquitting the condemned-prisoner and the other appellants from the charge levelled against them. 

 13. Now, let the evidence on record be carefully scrutinized and critically analyzed for determination whether the prosecution could prove beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused had committed the offence punishable under sections 302/34 and 459 of the Penal Code. 

 14. PW 1 Jesmin Akter, the informant of this case and daughter of the deceased Alauddin stated that in the night following 26-2-2001 at 12-30 AM accused Samjid Ali @ Katai, Koyes Ahmed, Mukit, Joynal Uddin, Abedin Ali, Mahmud Ali, Manik Miah, Abdus Sattar @ Bochai, Jamal, Jabbar, Kalai, Abdur Rouf along with 4/5 others breaking the door of the house had entered into their house, the accused were armed with gun, dao, dagger, rod etc, they caused a blank shot and hearing their alarm, her father came to them from the room of southern side. Accused Samjid Ali @ Katai targeting her father made the utterance— 

 15. At that time accused Koyes Ahmed, Jayonal, Abedin Ali, Mukit, Mahmud All had picked up her father and brought him into the room of western side. Accused Samjid Ali @ Katai fired gun on the right chest of her father causing him to instant death. She had identified the accused in the light of electricity and also in the light of torch used by the accused. Thereafter, the accused had left the house of occurrence. Hearing their alarms, the neighbouring people had come in the place of occurrence to whom they narrated the occurrence. She also stated that accused Koyes, Abedin, Samjid Ali @ Katai and others had kidnapped her younger sister Juron Begum and her mother filed a case being Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Case No. 89 of 2001 against the accused. Since her father coming into Bangladesh from abroad did not withdraw the said case, the accused had murder him. She identified the accused on dock save and except accused Mukit, Jabbar and Kalai. She further stated that she lodged First Information Report and she proved the same and her signature on it, marked as Exhibits-1 and 1/2. She also proved the inquest report and her signature on it, marked as Exhibits-2 and 2/1. 

 16. In cross-examination she stated that witness Hazi Hossain Ali and Hazi Amir Ali are the maternal uncle of her father, Lal Begum is her mother, Abdul Momin and Sayed Ali are her distant uncle, Shamsul Haque is her husband. She also stated that her marriage took place with Shamsul Haque in January, 2000, accused Samjid Ali @ Katai is the uncle of accused Koyes and the other accused are their relations, there are two barandas in their house, one is in the eastern side and another one is in the western side and between the two barandas there are two rooms in their house, one is in the northern side and another one is in the southern side. In the baranda of eastern side there is a collapsible gate. Amir Ali and Nimir Ali are the elites of their village. She denied the further defence suggestion that a dacoity took place two years ago in their house. She denied the defence suggestion that immediate after occurrence a declaration was given from the mike of a masjid that a dacoity has been committed in their house. 

 20. PW 5 Shamsul Haque, the husband of the informant stated that he coming in the house of his father-in-law at 4-00 PM on 26-2-2001 stayed there and in the night following 26-2-2001 at 12.30 AM accused Samjid Ali @ Katai, Koyes, Joynal, Abedin Ali, Mukit , Mahmud, Kalai, Abdul Jabbar and Abdur Rab being armed with gun, dao and bollom breaking the iron gate of the house had entered into the house. Accused Samjid Ali @ Katai caused blank shot. They had also assaulted him and whenever his father-in-law came into his room to save him accused Samjid Ali charged him as to why he did not withdraw the case. Thereafter, they picked up Alauddin and dragged him into the room of western side where accused Samjid Ali @ Katai fired gun on the right chest of the deceased. He further stated that Sarnjid Ali @ Katai was accompanied with the accused Joynal, Abedin and Mukit. His father-in-law met the death instantly in the place of occurrence for the gun shot injury which he received from accused Samjid Ali @ Katai. Hearing the alarm raised by them, the neighbouring people had rushed into the place of occurrence and heard the occurrence from them and also witnessed the same. He further stated that in the light of torch used by the accused he had identified the accused. The accused had kidnapped Juron Begum and his mother-in-law Lal Begum filed a case against the accused for that occurrence. The occurrence of murder of his father-in-law took place for not withdrawing the said case. In cross-examination he stated that his house is 5 miles away from the house of occurrence. He used to live in his own house with his wife. His father-in-law , used to sleep in the room of southern side and the other members of the house used to sleep in the room of northern side. The accused had entered into the house breaking the iron gate and the wooden door. The accused did not ranksack the household goods. On the following day at 10-00 AM the police came into the place of occurrence. He took treatment from Dr. Hamiduzzaman. At the time of occurrence there was the light of electricity in the house of occurrence and he had identified the accused in the light of electricity and also in the light of torch used by the accused. He denied the defence suggestion that the murder of his father-in-law had taken place at the time of committing docoity. 

 21. PW 6 Lal Begum, the wife of deceased Alauddin stated that in the night following 26-2-2001 at 12-30 AM accused Samjid Ali @ Katai, Mukit, Joynal, Mohammad Ali, Manik, Bochai, Abedin Ali, Kalai, Jabbar, Abdur Rab, Abedin, Jamal and Koyes being armed with gun, stick and sulfy forcibly entered into their house, accused Samjid Ali @ Katai caused a blank shot, they assaulted their son-in-law Shamsul Haque, 4/5 accused picked up her husband and dragged him into the room of western side where accused Samjid Ali @ Katai fired gun on the right chest of her husband causing the instant death of her husband. Hearing the alarm raised by them the neighbouring people had come into the place of occurrence whom they narrated the occurrence. She identified the accused in the dock save and except Mukit, Jabbar and Kalai. She adds that she filed a case against the accused for kidnapping her daughter Juron Begum. In cross-examination she stated that she and Alauddin were sleeping in the room of southern side while the rest were sleeping in the room of northern side. She having heard a sound of gun shot awoke from the sleeping. She went in the place of occurrence i.e. in the baranda of western side and the other inmates of the house also went there. There were six locks on the door. She cannot say what announcement was given by the mike from the mosque. She denied the defene suggestion that no occurrence was taken place as she had asserted. She also denied the further defence suggestion that the accused were not involved with the occurrence of murder of her husband. 

 29. PW 13 Jasim Uddin, the son of the deceased Alauddin stated that in the night following 26-2-2001 at 12-30 AM accused Samjid Ali @ Katai, Koyes, Mukit, Abedin, Joynal, Mahmud, Kalai, Jabbar breaking the iron grill and wooden door had entered into the house and caused a blank shot, accused Koyes, Abedin, Joynal and Kalai had picked up his father and dragged him into the kitchen where Samjid Ali fired gun on the right chest of his father. His father met instant death for the said gun injury. Thereafter, the accused-person left the place of occurrence. They had identified the accused in the light of electricity and light of torch. He had found accused Saimjid Ali @ Katai, Koyes, Abedin, Mukit, Joynal, Abdul Jabbar, Kalai, Mahmud and Abdur Rouf. In cross-examination he stated that he was younger to 4/5 years than that of his sister Juron Begum. He was a student of class four when his father was murdered. The kitchen is in the western side of the house. There is a hole on the door of the blank fire. At the time of firing on his father he was in the room of northern side, the other members of his family were also in the room of northern and southern side. He cannot say whether the accused fired the gun on his father touching the chest or not as he was not there. He denied the defence suggestion that he deposed falsely. 

 30. PW 14 Jany Begum, the daughter of deceased Alauddin stated that in the night following 26-2-2001 at 12-30 AM her father was murdered, accused Samjid Ali @ Katai, Koyes, Mukit, Joynal, Jabbar, Kalai, Abdul Sattar, Jamal, Abdur Rab along with 5-6 others breaking the gate of their house had entered into the house and they caused a blank shot. They took her father in the baranda thereafter fired gun causing the instant death of her father, hearing their alarm the local people came to their house to whom they narrated the occurrence. Since her father did not withdraw the case against the accused filed by her mother, the accused had murdered her father. In cross-examination she stated that at present she is twelve years and a student of class five and at the time of occurrence she was seven years when she used to sleep with her father. Her father used to sleep in the room of southern side while the other members used to sleep in the room of northern side. The accused caused the blank shot in the room of northern side. The blank shoot hit on a rain coat and the window also. She denied the defence suggestion that her sister had gone to Koyes voluntarily. She denied the further defence suggestion that accused are not connected with the murder of her father. 

 32. PW 16 Shamol Chandra Pual stated that on 27-2-2001 he was posted at Golapgonj Police Station as Sub-Inspector of Police, on that day he having got the FIR recorded the present case filing up the FIR columns. He proved the FIR columns and his signature in it, marked as Exhibit-3 and 3/1, he adds that the case was endorsed to him for investigation and at the initial stage of investigation he prepared the inquest report on the corpse of deceased Alauddin. He proved the same and his signature in it, marked as Exhibit 2 and 2/4. He further stated that the dead body of Alauddin was sent to Osmani Medical College Hospital for ascertaining the cause of death. He seized the rain coat, marked as material Exhibit-I; two locks, material Exhibit-II; two empty cartridges, material Exhibit-III; 15 pillets of firing, material Exhibit-IV under a seizure list. He proved the seizure list and his signature in it, marked as Exhibit-5 and 5/1. He further stated that he prepared sketch map and the index of the place of occurrence. He proved the sketch map and index, marked as Exhibits-6 & 7. He examined the witnesses and recorded their statement under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and pursuant to the order of his authority handed over the case docket on 1-3-2001 to the Officer-in-Charge. In cross-examination he stated that the occurrence of this case took place in the night following 26-2-2001 at 12-30 AM while the case was filed at 9-15 AM on 27-2-2001. He had reached in the place of occurrence at 10-45 AM on 27-2-2001 and returned back at 18-05 hours. He examined Hazi Hossain Ali, Lal Begum and Abdul Sayat on that date and recorded their statements also. In the inquest report he had stated that the deceased sustained gun injury. He himself seized the alamats. He found 15 pillets in the place of occurrence. He denied the defence suggestion that he did not seize the blood stained earth and the alamats have been created in order to provide support to the prosecution case. He further stated that witness Lal Begum did not tell the name of accused Mukit, Joynal, Mahmud, Manik, Kalai, Bochai, Jabbar, Abdur Rouf, Abedin, Jamal and Koyes to him. He also stated that Lal Begum also did not state to him that Samjid All caused a blank fire. She also did not state about the former case under Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain. He denied the defence suggestion that he did not record the statements of any disinterested witness and he also denied the defence suggestion that he did not investigate the case properly. 

 33. PW 17 and the last witness Md Shafiqul Islam stated that on 2-3-2001 he was posted as Officer-in-Charge at Golapgonj Police Station and he took the charge of investigation of this case on that date and before his investigation Police Sub-Inspector Shamol Chandra Poul had investigated the case. He had perused the investigation done by him who prepared the sketch map and index of the place of occurrence and she found the same as genuine. He recorded the statements of witnesses, arrested accused and procured the post-mortem examination report of the deceased and after completion of investigation submitted charge-sheet against the accused. In cross-examination he stated that he having got the charge of investigation on 2-3-2001 had visited the place of occurrence on the same day and returned back on 3-3-2001. He examined four witnesses on 28-3-2001 and recorded their statements also. He examined the accused on remand but could not recover anything from them. He did not seize any alamat at the time of investigation done by him. He denied the defence suggestion that he did not investigate the case properly and he being influenced by the prosecution submitted charge-sheet in this case. 

 35. Death of the deceased Alauddin in the night following 26-2-2001 in his dwelling but is not disputed in this case. According to the prosecution she was shot to death by the accused. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the convict appellants submits that deceased Alauddin has been suffering from some mental agony as his daughter Juron had left his house voluntarily and out of the said frustration he committed suicide in the house of occurrence but the informant using the death of her father entangled the accused with the occurrence of this case to take revenge against the accused. On appraisal of the evidence and other materials on record it appears that the fact of committing suicide by the deceased Alauddin has been presented by the learned Advocate of the appellant for the first time before us. No such case was made out ever before. The materials on record goes to show that there is no case that the deceased had any gun of his own rather it reavels that he was not a solvent man at all. He used to serve in the abroad for earning livelihood. So, his such economic condition did not permit him to have a gun or other short arms in his possession. On the other hand, PW 12 who held the post-mortem examination on the corpse of deceased Alauddin found a circular hole on the right side of the deceased 6 inches above the nipple with fracture of rib with ante-mortem haemorrhage clotted blood measuring 1½ inch square diameter and he recovered 29 pillets from the thoracic cavity of the deceased and in his opinion death was due to haemorrhage and shock as a result of fire arms injury which was ante-mortem and homicidal in nature. PW 12 was cross-examined extensively by defenc but his such evidence had not been shaken and shrunk away in any way, PWs 1, 5 ,6, 13 and 14 who are the inmates of the house of the deceased as ocular witnesses testified that the accused-person fired gun on the chest of the deceased. These prosecution witnesses were cross-examined by defence extensively but there is nothing in their cross-examination for which we can discard their such evidence. Thus the medical evidence is totally harmonica] with the evidence of PWs 1, 5, 6, 13 and 14 and the prosecution case that deceased was murdered by the gun shot. Thus, if we consider the medical evidence along with the evidence of the local witnesses and the other materials on record we find that deceased Alauddin was done to death in his house in the night following 26-2-2001. 

 36. Now, the moot question is who had committed the murder of deceased Alauddin? The simple prosecution case is that Alauddin was requested to withdraw the case filed by his wife against the accused for kidnapping his daughter Juron Begum and since he did not pay heed to the request of accused-persons they murdered him. PWs 1, 5, 6, 13 and 14 are the inmates of deceased Alauddin as well as eye-witnesses of the occurrence. PW 1 is the daughter, PW 5 is the son-in-law. PW 6 is the wife, PW 13 is the son and PW 14 is the another daughter of deceased Alauddin. These five prosecution witnesses as ocular witnesses very consistently stated before the trial court that the accused-persons breaking the iron gate and door had entered into the house and picking up the deceased Alauddin dragged him into the western baranda and firing gun on his chest murdered him. These five ocular witnesses categorically stated that accused Samjid Ali @ Katai had fired the gun on while accused Koyes, Abedin, Joynal, Kalai, Mukit, Mahmud picked up the deceased into the room of western side of the house. 

 38. We find that deceased Alauddin was murdered in the night at 12-30 in his own house providing no scope for others to witness the occurrence. It is not a case which took place between the two parties in the broad day light under the open sky in presence of the villagers or others rather it is a case where the occurrence of murder took place within a small house having two rooms and two barandas only in presence of the inhabitants of the said small house alone. So, there was no scope for others to be present there save and except the inmates of the house of occurrence and PWs 1, 5, 6, 13 and 14 as the inmates of the house of occurrence they are the most natural, probable and competent witnesses in this case. 

 "The conviction of the appellants can safely be based on the solitary evidence of the eye-witness, PW 1---------- His evidence is full, complete and self contained. It may not have received coroboration from other witnesses, but it stands fully corroborated by the circumstances of the case and the medical evidence on record. If this evidence is believed, and it has been rightly believed by both the Trial Court and the High Court Division, its fullness and completeness are enough to justify the conviction" (para 13 and 15 of the judgment). 

 "We have indicated earlier that she (PW 2) is the most natural, probable and competent witness in the present case as she was reading in the same room with her deceased sister Dilara and saw the entire occurrence. She has given details of the entire occurrence and even in her cross-examination the defence could not show any material discrepancy for which her ocular testimony should be disbelieved. She having deposed the entire incident from the beginning to the end it is very difficult for us to discard her evidence only on the ground that she was an interested witness and was a minor girl aged about 16 years. Even the law provides that a child witness can be relied if he/she is capable of understanding and replying the questions intelligently "(para 14 of the judgment). 

 51. The learned Advocate putting much emphasis on such evidence of PW 13 submits that the occurrence has not been witnessed by PW 13 as such he could not state as to how the gun shot was caused on the chest of deceased. It is fact that PW 13 could not state whether the gun had touched the chest of his father at the time of gun shot but it does not mean that he did not witness the occurrence of causing gun fire on his father. The occurrence of gun fire took place within a small room, so everybody may not get scope equally to visualize the trifling and negligible side of the occurrence. PW 14 Jani Begum, the another daughter of the deceased stated that accused Samjid Ali fired gun on her father causing him to death, PW 14 deposed in the Court below on 27-6-2005 when she was 12 years, so, at the time of occurrence which took place on 26-2-2001 she was a minor girl of 7-8 years. However, her evidence appears to have revealed the prudent picture of the occurrence which is consistent with the facts and circumstances of the case. Thus the evidence of ocular witnesses PWs 1, 5, 6, 13, 14 appears to be credible, unimpeachable and unshaken to us which are compatible and fit with the facts and circumstances of the case. They were elaborately and very vividly cross-examined by the defence but there appears no ingredients of false evidence and sign of emotion and biasness in their such evidence. All the ocular witnesses very consistently stated that Samjid Ali @ Katai fired gun on the right chest of the deceased and this evidence is very much harmonical with the medical evidence on record. Moreso PWs 2, 3, 4 who are the neighbours of the deceased stated that immediate after occurrence they having been in the place of occurrence heard the occurrence from the informant and other inmates of the house of the occurrence that Samjid Ali @ Katai had fired gun on the deceased causing him to death. PWs 2 and 3 are the maternal uncle of the deceased but PW 4 is a distant relation of the informant. Though PWs 2 and 3 are maternal uncles of the deceased but at the same time they are the close door neighbours and local elites of the village, so both the PWs 2, 3 and 4 very much natural and probable witnesses of this case who heard the occurrence and the name of accused from the eye-witness immediate after occurrence. Now, if we consider the evidence of the eye-witnesses along with the evidence PWs 2, 3 and 4 who without any late immediate after occurrence rushed to the place of occurrence and heard the occurrence and name of the killer from the ocular witnesses there would have no better alternative but to find accused Samjid Ali @ Katai as killer of the deceased who fired gun on the right chest of the deceased causing him to death. So, the court below on the correct assessment of evidences on record rightly found Samjid Ali @ Katai guilty under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code. 

 52. It is the prosecution case that accused Koyes, Mukit Abedin, Joynal and Mahmud had picked up the deceased and dragged him into the room of western side where he was murdered. PWs 1 and 13 stated that accused Koyes, Abedin and Joynal had picked up the deceased and dragged him into the room of western side where the deceased was murdered. PW 1 stated that Mukit also picked up his father and dragged him into room of western side. PW 5 stated that at the time of murder Abedin, Joynal and Mukit were present with accused Samjid Ali @ Katai. 

 53. In the case of Abu Sayed vs State, 38 DLR 17, it was held that for the applicability of section 34 it is essential that the act of murder is done by several persons. In other words, all the persons who were sought to be made liable by virtue of section 34 must have done some act and those of the accused who had not taken any part either by word or action in doing the act of murder cannot be made liable under that section. The trial court found accused Koyes, Abedin, Joynal and Mukit guilty under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code as they had shared their common intention to murder the deceased with the other accused. The evidence on record goes to show that accused Koyes Abedin, Joynal and Mukit had picked up the deceased and dragged him into the room of western side where the deceased was murdered is an act of participation in the commission of murder of the deceased and their such act has established and proved that they had the common intention to murder the deceased and in pursuant to the said common intention they had picked up the deceased and dragged him into the room of the western side where the murderous gun shot was caused on the deceased. So, the trial court also on the right assessment of the evidence on record found Koyes, Abedin and Joynal guilty under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code for causing murder of the deceased Alauddin. 

 55. PWs 1, 5, 6, 13 and 14 in a chorus voice testified that the accused-persons particularly accused Samjid Ali @ Katai charged the deceased as to why he did not withdraw the case. It is the prosecution case that the wife of deceased filed a case against the accused for the abduction of her daughter Juron Begum and this fact has been proved by PW 7 Juron Begum herself. The very utterance of Samjid Ali @ Katai charging the deceased that as to why he did not withdraw the case had itself disclosed the identification of the accused. So, from the materials on record it reavels that the accused-person themselves had disclosed their identity to the witnesses. So, there is no scope to hold that the recognization of the accused is doubtful in this case. 

 59. The evidence on record goes to show that at the time of house breaking their took place no resistance at all. So the occurrence of house breaking by the accused in order to commit the murder of deceased provides no room for application of section 459 of the Penal Code. From the materials on record it clearly shows that at the time of house breaking, the accused did not cause hurt to anybody, so, the very framing of charge under section 459 of the Penal Code against accused Samjid Ali @ Katai, Koyes, Abedin and Joynal was misapplication of law as well as conviction of sentence upon these 4 accused under section 459 is not maintainable in the eye of law. 

 61. Having regards to the facts and circumstances of the case and the discussion made above we find that the trial court on the correct assessment of the evidences on record rightly found accused Samjid Ali @ Katai guilty under section 302 of the Penal Code for causing murder of deceased Alauddin, 

 62. The facts and circumstances of the case goes to show that Samjid Ali @ Katai and others committed a cold blooded murder of deceased Alauddin and in a preplanned way they had entered into the house of the deceased and in execution of their such premediated device murdered the 9 deceased. So, in the case of the State vs Rokeya 11 MLR 63 = 10 BLC 687 it was held that in a cold blooded murder, death is the proper sentence. We find that the trial court considering the facts and attending circumstances of the case and the evidence and other materials on record rightly awarded death sentence to accused Samjid Ali @ Katai. And considering the materials and evidence on record rightly found accused Koyes, Joynal and Abedin guilty under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and rightly awarded imprisonment for life with a fine of Taka 5,000 to these three accused.
